questions.question: Why is the triangle inequality considered a norm property?
options: It says the zero vector has no coordinates.
It makes every vector have length one.
It controls the norm of a sum by the sum of the norms.
questions.explanation: A norm must be subadditive: the length assigned to a sum is bounded by the sum of the assigned lengths. This is exactly the triangle inequality.
